sentences.text: Something can be beautiful enough to hold your attention and still deserve your rejection.
sentences.approvedCue: Place an attractive public spectacle beside a viewer whose expression remains troubled.

sentences.text: Beauty: The Anatomy of Fascination explores the attraction that makes that tension possible.
sentences.approvedCue: Hold the viewer’s attention without turning their attraction into a sign of approval.

sentences.text: It moves from an elegant proof to an intimate face, and from music to political spectacle.
sentences.approvedCue: Cut between an elegant proof, an intimate sleeping face, a musical phrase and the public spectacle.

sentences.text: These encounters ask what beauty shows us, what we add to it, and what admiration can excuse.
sentences.approvedCue: Keep the admired object visible while a separate question asks what admiration excuses.

sentences.text: The book connects philosophy with psychology, culture, bodies, and the histories of familiar objects.
sentences.approvedCue: Show a familiar object with traces of use and cultural history rather than an isolated beauty score.

sentences.text: An inherited possession and its perfect copy can look alike while offering different experiences.
sentences.approvedCue: Place the inherited object beside a precise copy, letting their histories remain different.

sentences.text: An attraction you struggled to explain becomes a reason to look more closely.
sentences.approvedCue: Let a viewer return to one personally meaningful object and look more closely.

sentences.text: Begin with the opening encounters, and look again at something you already find beautiful.
sentences.approvedCue: End with the object still held in attention, leaving room for both pleasure and judgment.
